document.title_main: - Business Requirements Specification for Jaywan Domestic Card Scheme Enablement and Co‑Badged Card Issuance
document.program: - Jaywan Domestic Card Scheme – Mono-Badged and Co-Badged Cards Enablement
document.overview:
- Jaywan is the UAE’s first domestic card scheme operated by Al Etihad Payments (AEP), a subsidiary of the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE)
- The CBUAE has mandated licensed Financial Institutions (FIs) to support Jaywan domestic card transactions in line with national payment strategy and financial sovereignty objectives
- The scheme supports mono-badged domestic and GCC usage cards, and co-badged cards in partnership with international payment networks for local and international usage
- The payment infrastructure has been confirmed as ready by AEP to activate Jaywan locally and globally, including upcoming enablement on Samsung Wallet, Google Pay, and Apple Pay
- The initiative aims to reduce domestic payment costs, improve routing efficiency, and provide a secure, seamless, and inclusive payment experience to consumers and corporates
- Discovery sessions and working meetings between Business, IT, Card Operations, Finance, and external stakeholders (including AEP and international schemes) are ongoing to refine requirements for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged cards
document.current_constraint:
- The bank currently issues international scheme cards (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) without Jaywan co-badging in line with past practices
- Existing card management, authorization, clearing, settlement, and GL setup are designed primarily for international schemes and do not natively support Jaywan routing, fees, and reporting structures
- Current domestic e-commerce and tokenization flows are based on existing VISA DMS and do not fully reflect the future CBUAE/AEP DMS model for Jaywan
- POS tokenized transactions under Jaywan have not yet been fully defined and may not be included in current solution scope or impact assessment
- Reversal, refund, and chargeback processes for Jaywan transactions are not fully aligned with AEP’s operating rules and are still under clarification
- Reconciliation documentation and reporting templates from CBUAE/AEP are in progress and require further analysis before full automation
- Some bilateral cross-border enablement aspects (e.g. India by mid-2025 and other countries) are still being defined at scheme level, constraining detailed requirements
document.objective:
- CBUAE has issued a mandate that all licensed financial institutions shall launch Jaywan co-badged cards in compliance with the Central Bank circular (reference 5480/2024 as provided in context)
- Banks issuing Mastercard or Visa cards shall, for eligible portfolios, issue co-badged cards that support both domestic transactions via Jaywan and international transactions via the relevant international scheme
- Card routing shall be configured to ensure domestic transactions are processed via Jaywan and international transactions via the selected international scheme, in line with CBUAE and AEP guidance
- The bank shall enable issuance and lifecycle management of Jaywan mono-badged cards for domestic and GCC usage where business decides to support such portfolios
- The bank shall ensure readiness of systems, operations, finance, risk, and customer channels to support Jaywan transactions across POS, ATM, e-commerce, tokenized payments, and contactless mobile wallets
- The bank shall comply with CBUAE and AEP regulations, technical standards, and reporting obligations related to the Jaywan scheme and domestic card processing
- The bank shall leverage Jaywan to support reduction of domestic payment acceptance and issuance costs and to maintain a secure and seamless payment experience for customers and merchants
document.in_scope:
- Definition and implementation of business requirements for Jaywan mono-badged cards for domestic and GCC usage
- Definition and implementation of business requirements for Jaywan co-badged cards with international schemes (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) for domestic and international usage
- Configuration of routing logic to prioritize Jaywan for domestic UAE transactions and applicable GCC transactions, and to route international transactions via the designated international scheme
- Alignment of dual messaging system processes for Jaywan (authorization, clearing, settlement) similar to existing VISA DMS where applicable and as permitted by AEP
- Definition of to-be process flows for ATM, POS, e-commerce, and tokenized transactions under the Jaywan scheme, including CBUAE DMS for e-commerce and tokenization
- Inclusion and impact assessment of POS tokenized transactions for Jaywan where required by business and regulators
- GL account structure, posting rules, and reconciliation approach for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged transactions, as confirmed with Finance
- Impact assessment and definition of business rules for reversals, refunds, and chargebacks for Jaywan in line with AEP rules
- Customer communication and support readiness related to Jaywan product features, fees, and dispute handling
- Reporting requirements to CBUAE/AEP and internal stakeholders (Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Business) for Jaywan transaction monitoring and reconciliation
- Support for enablement of Jaywan cards in digital wallets (Samsung Wallet initially, then Google Pay and Apple Pay) as the scheme and bank become ready
- Coordination with AEP and other stakeholders on open questions, clarifications, and adoption of standard documents (process, file formats, operating rules)
document.out_of_scope:
- Detailed technical design, low-level system design, and code-level specifications for Jaywan integration
- Negotiation of commercial interchange rates, scheme fees, or bilateral commercial terms with AEP or international schemes
- Non-card payment instruments such as instant payments, direct debits, and wire transfers outside the Jaywan card scheme
- Detailed design of bilateral international corridor arrangements beyond high-level requirements (e.g. specific India corridor configuration and pricing)
- Changes to existing non-card-related GL structures and accounting policies not directly impacted by Jaywan
- Enterprise-wide changes to AML, sanctions, and fraud platforms beyond necessary parameterization to recognize and monitor Jaywan transactions
- Marketing campaign content design beyond high-level requirements for awareness and communication alignment with AEP

business_requirements.title_bs: - Jaywan Co-Badged Card Issuance Mandate Compliance
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall comply with the CBUAE mandate requiring issuance of Jaywan co-badged cards alongside existing international schemes for eligible portfolios
- The bank shall ensure that newly issued cards for relevant product lines are co-badged with Jaywan and at least one international scheme (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) as per regulatory circular
- The bank shall maintain alignment with CBUAE circular reference provided (5480/2024 as per context) and any subsequent updates shared formally by the regulator or AEP
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- The bank issues single-badged international scheme cards (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) for debit, credit, and prepaid products without Jaywan branding or routing
- Domestic and international transactions are both processed via the respective international scheme, subject to acquirer routing and scheme rules
- Existing product setup, card BIN ranges, and customer communication are aligned solely to international scheme requirements
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall issue co-badged cards for defined portfolios where the card carries both Jaywan and the selected international scheme marks
- The bank shall ensure that the card BINs and card profiles support domestic routing via Jaywan and international routing via the respective scheme as per CBUAE and AEP guidance
- The bank shall define which existing and new products will migrate to or be launched as Jaywan co-badged cards in line with regulatory timelines
- The bank shall ensure customer onboarding, card fulfilment, and lifecycle management processes explicitly recognize the co-badged nature of the card
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- CBUAE circular and AEP implementation guidelines shall be reviewed and formally acknowledged by Compliance and Legal
- AEP shall provide the bank with Jaywan-specific BIN allocation, branding specifications, and operating rules
- International schemes shall confirm co-badging rules and any restrictions for use of their marks alongside Jaywan
- Internal product governance and approval processes shall endorse the move to co-badged portfolio structures
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- All new cards in defined portfolios shall be issued as Jaywan co-badged cards after the effective date approved by Business and Compliance
- Card plastics and digital card art shall display Jaywan and the selected international scheme marks in accordance with branding guidelines
- The product catalogue shall list Jaywan co-badged variants for the relevant debit, credit, and prepaid offerings
- Compliance shall confirm that issuance practices align with CBUAE circular requirements and that no non-compliant single-badged international cards are issued in the in-scope portfolios
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- Certain niche or exceptional products may remain as single-badged international scheme cards where permitted by CBUAE and AEP, subject to explicit regulatory approval
- For legacy portfolios where immediate migration is not feasible, the bank may phase in co-badged issuance upon expiry or replacement of existing cards, subject to a documented migration plan
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- CBUAE Circular – Jaywan Co-Badged Card Mandate (reference 5480/2024 as per provided context)
- AEP Jaywan Scheme Operating Rules and Branding Guidelines
- Internal Product Approval and Governance Policy
- Meeting minutes and discovery sessions related to Jaywan co-badged card requirements

business_requirements.title_bs: - Jaywan Mono-Badged Card Issuance for Domestic and GCC Usage
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall support issuance of Jaywan mono-badged cards for domestic and eligible GCC usage as per AEP guidelines
- Jaywan mono-badged cards shall be designed to operate without an international scheme companion badge and shall be restricted to geo-zones defined by AEP and the bank’s risk policy
- The bank shall position Jaywan mono-badged cards for specific customer segments or use cases based on business strategy and regulatory expectations
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- The bank does not currently issue Jaywan mono-badged cards and relies solely on international scheme cards for all usage
- Domestic and GCC usage is facilitated via international schemes with associated cost and dependency implications
- No dedicated mono-badged domestic card proposition exists in the product catalogue
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall create at least one Jaywan mono-badged card product for domestic transactions and GCC usage where supported by the scheme
- The bank shall configure card parameters, usage restrictions, and pricing for Jaywan mono-badged cards in line with CBUAE and AEP expectations
- The bank shall ensure that mono-badged Jaywan cards are recognized across internal systems (card management, authorization, GL, reporting) as a distinct scheme and product type
- The bank shall define clear customer communication on usage limitations (e.g. no non-GCC international transactions) where applicable
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP shall confirm the rules for GCC acceptance and any bilateral or regional arrangements relevant to Jaywan mono-badged cards
- The Finance team shall confirm GL accounts and fee structures applicable to mono-badged domestic and GCC transactions
- Risk and Compliance shall approve customer eligibility criteria and usage restrictions for mono-badged products
- Card personalization and embossing specifications for mono-badged Jaywan cards shall be finalized with card vendors
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- At least one Jaywan mono-badged card product shall be defined and approved in the product catalogue
- Test cards for mono-badged Jaywan products shall successfully perform domestic and approved GCC test transactions during UAT
- Customer-facing documentation and disclosures shall clearly explain the geographic usage scope of Jaywan mono-badged cards
- Internal systems shall correctly classify and report transactions on mono-badged Jaywan cards as domestic or GCC in alignment with AEP guidance
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If GCC enablement is not available at initial launch, the bank may launch mono-badged Jaywan cards with UAE-only usage and later extend to GCC based on scheme readiness
- The bank may restrict mono-badged issuance to selected segments initially (e.g. basic accounts, payroll) and expand progressively based on performance and regulatory feedback
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP Jaywan Scheme Guidelines for Mono-Badged Cards
- CBUAE Policy Papers on Domestic Card Schemes and GCC Usage
- Internal Product Strategy Documents for Domestic Card Offerings
- Discovery session minutes on Jaywan mono-badged requirements

business_requirements.title_bs: - Domestic and International Transaction Routing for Jaywan Co-Badged Cards
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall implement routing logic ensuring that domestic UAE transactions on co-badged cards are processed via Jaywan while international transactions are processed via the relevant international scheme
- The bank shall comply with CBUAE and AEP requirements on mandatory use of Jaywan for domestic transactions where acceptance infrastructure is available
- The bank shall ensure routing rules are consistently applied across POS, ATM, e-commerce, and tokenized channels where technically feasible
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Domestic and international transactions on existing cards are routed based on international scheme rules and acquirer configuration without Jaywan considerations
- The bank’s authorization and switch systems apply scheme selection based primarily on BIN and acquirer data for international schemes only
- There is no dedicated domestic scheme routing logic specific to Jaywan within current system configurations
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall configure authorization and switch systems so that domestic UAE transactions on Jaywan co-badged cards default to Jaywan routing when the merchant/acquirer supports Jaywan
- The bank shall ensure that cross-border transactions (outside UAE, and as applicable outside GCC) on co-badged cards are routed via the designated international scheme
- The bank shall define clear exception handling rules where Jaywan is not available at the merchant/acquirer, including fallback to the international scheme where permitted by regulation
- The bank shall coordinate with acquiring partners and AEP to validate that routing behavior aligns with domestic scheme objectives and regulatory expectations
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP shall provide technical specifications and routing rules for Jaywan, including domestic acceptance parameters and MCC or geo-based rules where applicable
- International schemes shall confirm co-badge routing principles and any constraints on domestic routing prioritization
- The bank’s switch and authorization system owners shall confirm technical feasibility and configuration approach for multi-scheme routing
- End-to-end test plans shall be defined to validate routing behavior under multiple domestic and international scenarios
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Domestic test transactions on co-badged cards at Jaywan-enabled merchants shall be processed via Jaywan as evidenced by scheme identifiers in logs and reports
- International test transactions on co-badged cards shall be processed via the correct international scheme with accurate scheme identifiers
- Fallback scenarios where Jaywan is not supported at the merchant/acquirer shall follow the defined exception logic and be traceable in logs
- Compliance and AEP shall confirm routing behavior meets regulatory and scheme expectations as part of launch readiness sign-off
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- In rare cases where technical limitations at a particular channel prevent Jaywan routing, the bank may temporarily route via the international scheme subject to documented risk assessment and regulatory notification where required
- For certain cross-border GCC transactions, routing may follow specific corridor rules as defined by AEP and international agreements
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP Jaywan Technical and Routing Specifications
- International Scheme Co-Badge Routing Guidelines
- Bank Switch and Authorization System Configuration Standards
- Discovery session minutes on VISA DMS processes and adoption for Jaywan

business_requirements.title_bs: - Dual Messaging and DMS Process Alignment for Jaywan
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall align its dual messaging (authorization and clearing) processes for Jaywan with CBUAE and AEP requirements, leveraging existing VISA DMS experience where applicable
- The bank shall define and document to-be process flows for Jaywan across ATM, POS, e-commerce, and tokenized channels under the CBUAE DMS framework
- The bank shall ensure that all impacted operational units (Card Operations, GBO-ATM/CDM, Reconciliation) understand and adopt the new Jaywan DMS processes
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Current SMS processes exist for ATM and POS under existing schemes
- VISA DMS processes are implemented for VISA e-commerce and tokenization transactions
- A to-be CBUAE DMS model for domestic e-commerce and tokenization transactions is documented but not fully implemented for Jaywan
- Operational teams follow existing scheme-specific workflows for authorizations, clearings, reversals, and exceptions
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall implement Jaywan DMS processes that cover authorization, clearing, reversal, and settlement flows consistent with AEP specifications
- The bank shall document end-to-end to-be flows for Jaywan across ATM, POS, e-commerce, and tokenized channels, including reconciliation touchpoints
- The bank shall ensure that Jaywan-specific message formats, timelines, and cut-offs are embedded into operational procedures
- The bank shall adopt standardized approaches where possible by re-using and adapting existing VISA DMS process patterns to minimize complexity while staying within scheme rules
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP shall provide final Jaywan message formats, DMS rules, and settlement cycles
- Business and IT teams shall validate and update documented process flows for current SMS, existing VISA DMS, and to-be CBUAE DMS to incorporate Jaywan
- Card Operations, GBO-ATM/CDM, and Reconciliation teams shall review and confirm their roles and responsibilities in the to-be Jaywan processes
- System impact assessments shall identify required changes to switching, card host, reconciliation tools, and GL posting engines
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Approved and version-controlled process flow documents shall exist for Jaywan DMS across all in-scope channels
- UAT shall demonstrate successful end-to-end processing for Jaywan authorization, clearing, and settlement scenarios, including reversals and exceptions
- Operational runbooks shall be updated to include Jaywan-specific steps and controls
- Internal audit or process assurance shall confirm that Jaywan DMS processes are clearly defined and aligned with regulatory expectations
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- For certain low-volume channels, the bank may temporarily follow semi-manual or hybrid processes for Jaywan clearings, subject to risk acceptance and a plan to automate in subsequent phases
- For exceptional cross-border flows where Jaywan interacts with other domestic schemes, specific bilateral DMS arrangements may be documented separately
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Documented process flows for current SMS and VISA DMS (e-commerce and tokenization)
- Draft and final CBUAE DMS specifications for domestic transactions
- AEP Jaywan Operating Rules and Message Specifications
- Minutes from discovery session with Card Operations, GBO-ATM/CDM, and Business

business_requirements.title_bs: - Inclusion of POS Tokenized Transactions for Jaywan
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall consider POS tokenized transactions within the scope of Jaywan enablement where required by the business and supported by AEP
- The bank shall ensure that tokenized POS transactions on Jaywan cards, including contactless and mobile wallet transactions, are processed securely and in compliance with scheme and regulatory requirements
- The bank shall align the treatment of POS tokenized transactions under Jaywan with existing practices for VISA DMS tokenized transactions where possible
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- VISA DMS is in place for VISA e-commerce and tokenization transactions
- POS tokenized transactions are handled under existing international scheme frameworks and are not explicitly defined for Jaywan
- Business stakeholders have raised that POS tokenized transactions may need to be in scope for Jaywan but final decision and design are pending
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall define whether POS tokenized transactions are in scope for Jaywan in the initial phase and document this decision formally
- Where in scope, the bank shall configure systems and processes so that POS tokenized Jaywan transactions follow secure tokenization, routing, and DMS rules compliant with AEP
- The bank shall ensure contactless and mobile wallet usage of Jaywan cards at POS is supported in line with scheme and wallet provider requirements
- The bank shall ensure consistent customer experience and dispute handling for tokenized and non-tokenized Jaywan transactions
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP shall confirm tokenization standards, supported token requestors, and POS tokenization rules for Jaywan
- Wallet providers (e.g. Samsung, Google, Apple) shall confirm technical integration and scheme support for Jaywan
- Information Security and Risk stakeholders shall review tokenization risk controls for Jaywan
- Business and IT shall agree on the go-live scope for POS tokenized transactions under Jaywan
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- A formal scope decision document shall state inclusion or phased inclusion of POS tokenized transactions for Jaywan
- Where in scope, POS tokenized Jaywan test transactions shall be successfully executed in UAT and reflect accurate routing, tokenization, and posting
- Customer support scripts shall address POS tokenized Jaywan card queries, including lost devices and token lifecycle events
- No unresolved high-risk security or compliance issues shall remain for POS tokenized Jaywan transactions at go-live
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If POS tokenized transactions are deferred, Jaywan enablement shall initially focus on physical card transactions and may enable POS tokenization in a subsequent phase with separate requirements
- Certain wallet providers may be enabled at different times (e.g. Samsung Wallet first, then Google Pay and Apple Pay) based on scheme readiness and commercial agreements
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Existing VISA DMS tokenization transaction process documentation
- AEP Jaywan Tokenization and Mobile Wallet Guidelines (to be obtained)
- Internal Tokenization and Digital Wallet Policies
- Meeting minutes highlighting POS tokenized transaction scope considerations

business_requirements.title_bs: - GL Accounting and Reconciliation for Jaywan Transactions
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall implement dedicated GL structures and reconciliation processes for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged transactions in line with Finance team confirmation
- The bank shall ensure that all Jaywan-related financial entries (fees, interchange, chargebacks, refunds, reversals) are accurately posted and reconciled
- The bank shall align reconciliation reporting with CBUAE and AEP formats provided
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Finance has confirmed that GL details are prepared based on internal discussions, but Jaywan-specific postings are not yet in production
- Current reconciliation processes and reports are centered around international schemes and existing domestic flows
- Queries have been raised regarding reconciliation documentation and original reports from CBUAE, some of which have now been shared
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall configure GL accounts for Jaywan scheme settlement, income, and expense categories as approved by Finance
- The bank shall implement automated reconciliation processes for Jaywan that match scheme files, bank records, and GL entries
- The bank shall generate reconciliation reports aligned with CBUAE/AEP templates and internal MIS needs for Jaywan portfolios
- The bank shall incorporate Jaywan-related reversals, refunds, and chargebacks in accounting logic based on finalized operational and scheme rules
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Finance shall finalize and sign off GL account mapping and posting rules for Jaywan
- CBUAE/AEP shall provide original reconciliation report formats and data field definitions
- System teams shall confirm capability of reconciliation tools to ingest Jaywan files
- Operations and Finance shall agree on reconciliation responsibilities and timelines
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- GL posting rules for Jaywan shall be documented and validated through test cycles involving sample transactions and settlement files
- Reconciliation for Jaywan pilot or test batches shall show no unexplained variances after adjustments
- CBUAE/AEP and internal stakeholders shall receive agreed reports accurately reflecting Jaywan transaction and settlement positions
- Finance shall sign off on readiness of GL and reconciliation processes prior to go-live
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- Initially, partial manual reconciliation may be used for low-volume Jaywan transactions subject to documented controls and a plan for full automation
- Some fee components or adjustments may be grouped at higher levels initially and later broken down as data quality and volumes mature
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Finance-confirmed GL Account Details for Jaywan (internal)
- CBUAE/AEP Reconciliation Report Templates and Specifications
- Internal Reconciliation Policy and Procedure Manuals
- Email communications and minutes referencing GL readiness and reconciliation documentation

business_requirements.title_bs: - Reversals, Refunds, and Chargebacks for Jaywan Transactions
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall define and implement business rules and operational processes for processing reversals, refunds, and chargebacks for Jaywan transactions
- The bank shall ensure that these dispute and adjustment processes comply with AEP and CBUAE guidelines and are aligned with customer protection standards
- The bank shall provide clear customer communication and support for Jaywan-related disputes and adjustments
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Existing reversals, refunds, and chargebacks are executed based on international scheme rules and internal policies
- Jaywan-specific reversal, refund, and chargeback processes are under discussion and partially clarified in meetings but not fully finalized
- Operational teams rely on scheme documentation and experience from international schemes without dedicated Jaywan procedures
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall document end-to-end processes for Jaywan reversals, refunds, and chargebacks, including timelines, evidentiary requirements, and liability rules
- The bank shall configure systems to process Jaywan dispute transactions with proper scheme identifiers and GL impacts
- The bank shall train dispute handling teams on Jaywan rules and ensure they can distinguish between Jaywan and international scheme disputes for co-badged cards
- The bank shall ensure that regulatory timelines for consumer dispute resolution under Jaywan are met and monitored
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP shall issue detailed dispute and chargeback rules for Jaywan, including reason codes and lifecycle stages
- Legal and Compliance shall review Jaywan dispute rules and align them with local consumer protection requirements
- Card Operations and Dispute Management teams shall participate in process design workshops for Jaywan
- Systems shall be assessed for capabilities to support Jaywan-specific dispute codes and workflows
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Approved operating procedures for Jaywan reversals, refunds, and chargebacks shall be published for relevant teams
- UAT scenarios shall validate at least one end-to-end case each for reversal, refund, and chargeback under Jaywan
- Dispute dashboards or reports shall allow segregation and monitoring of Jaywan cases and compliance with turnaround times
- No critical gaps shall be identified by Compliance or Internal Audit regarding dispute handling for Jaywan
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- In early phases, certain complex dispute scenarios may be handled with additional manual review steps until full automation is delivered
- For co-badged cards, some disputes may be managed through the international scheme where the transaction was processed outside Jaywan’s acceptance domain
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP Jaywan Dispute and Chargeback Rules (to be provided)
- Existing Bank Dispute Management Policies for Card Transactions
- Meeting minutes referencing updates on reversals, refunds, and chargebacks for Jaywan
- CBUAE Consumer Protection Regulations relevant to card disputes

business_requirements.title_bs: - Reporting and Regulatory Submissions for Jaywan
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall implement reporting capabilities to meet CBUAE and AEP reporting obligations for Jaywan transactions and scheme participation
- The bank shall update internal MIS and operational reports to include Jaywan-specific metrics for monitoring performance, risk, and compliance
- The bank shall ensure that reports used for reconciliation, risk management, and business decision-making reflect Jaywan volumes and values separately from other schemes where required
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Queries have been clarified with business regarding existing reports, and an original report from CBUAE has been shared for reference
- Current reporting structures primarily focus on international schemes and existing domestic flows without Jaywan segmentation
- Some documentation on reconciliation and reporting is still being requested and reviewed by stakeholders
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall design Jaywan-specific regulatory reports aligned with templates and data definitions from CBUAE/AEP
- The bank shall enhance existing internal reports (e.g. daily settlement, scheme performance, fraud monitoring) to include Jaywan as a separate scheme or category
- The bank shall ensure that reports support analysis of Jaywan’s impact on payment costs, transaction volumes, and customer adoption
- The bank shall validate that data lineage and quality controls are in place for all Jaywan-related reporting fields
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- CBUAE/AEP shall provide finalized reporting templates, including frequency, thresholds, and submission channels
- Data owners shall confirm source systems and data elements required for Jaywan reporting
- BI and Reporting teams shall assess impact on existing report generation platforms
- Business and Compliance shall review and approve final report definitions and layouts
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- All mandatory Jaywan regulatory reports shall be produced in test cycles and validated by Compliance and AEP where applicable
- Internal MIS reports shall display Jaywan metrics distinctly and accurately for at least one full reporting period in trial run
- No critical reconciliation gaps shall appear between Jaywan scheme reports and internal ledgers
- Report submission timelines and controls shall be documented and adhered to for at least one full cycle before go-live
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- Where full automation is not feasible initially, interim spreadsheets or semi-manual extracts may be used for low-volume Jaywan reporting with appropriate controls
- Some less critical internal dashboards may be implemented after go-live as a subsequent enhancement phase
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- CBUAE/AEP Jaywan Reporting Templates and Guidelines
- Internal MIS and Regulatory Reporting Policies
- Email communications confirming receipt of original CBUAE report formats
- Discovery session minutes addressing report requirements and clarifications

business_requirements.title_bs: - Digital Wallet and Tokenization Enablement for Jaywan
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall enable Jaywan card provisioning into supported digital wallets in alignment with scheme roadmap (Samsung Wallet initially, followed by Google Pay and Apple Pay)
- The bank shall ensure that wallet-based transactions on Jaywan cards provide a secure, seamless payment experience consistent with AEP and wallet provider requirements
- The bank shall support consumer awareness and usage of Jaywan in digital wallets as part of wider adoption initiatives
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Existing wallet integrations (if any) are oriented around international schemes and may not currently recognize Jaywan as a distinct scheme
- Jaywan readiness for Samsung Wallet has been announced at ecosystem level, with further enablement for Google Pay and Apple Pay in the next phase
- The bank’s current product and operations documentation does not fully cover Jaywan wallet usage scenarios
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall configure digital wallet integration such that Jaywan cards can be tokenized, provisioned, and used across supported devices and form factors
- The bank shall ensure that transaction routing from wallets follows Jaywan domestic routing rules where applicable
- The bank shall define operational procedures for managing wallet tokens, including activation, suspension, de-provisioning, and lost or stolen devices for Jaywan cards
- The bank shall align customer education materials with AEP’s awareness campaign to highlight Jaywan wallet features and benefits
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- AEP and wallet providers shall confirm technical specifications, certification requirements, and go-live timelines for Jaywan enablement on each wallet
- Information Security shall review and approve security controls for tokenized Jaywan wallet transactions
- Channels and Digital Banking teams shall ensure that mobile and online channels display Jaywan wallet functionality correctly
- Customer support teams shall be briefed on common wallet-related use cases and issues for Jaywan
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Jaywan cards shall be successfully provisioned to at least one wallet (e.g. Samsung Wallet) in pilot testing and used for live test transactions
- Wallet transactions using Jaywan cards shall be correctly reflected in transaction history, GL, and reports with appropriate scheme identification
- Customer-facing FAQs and guides on Jaywan wallet usage shall be published and accessible
- No high-risk security or stability issues shall be identified in penetration and performance tests for Jaywan wallet transactions
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If certain wallets are not ready for Jaywan at project go-live, the bank may prioritize one wallet first and roll out to others in subsequent phases with separate readiness assessments
- For customers on devices not supporting relevant wallets, Jaywan functionality shall remain available via physical cards and non-wallet channels
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP Jaywan Roadmap for Digital Wallet Enablement
- Wallet Provider Integration Guides for Jaywan (Samsung, Google, Apple)
- Internal Digital Banking and Tokenization Standards
- AEP public communications on wallet enablement and awareness campaigns

business_requirements.title_bs: - Governance, Discovery Sessions, and Stakeholder Alignment for Jaywan Implementation
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall maintain a structured governance framework and discovery session schedule to capture and refine additional requirements for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged cards
- The bank shall ensure alignment between Business, IT, Card Operations, Finance, Risk, and external stakeholders (AEP, schemes) throughout implementation
- The bank shall document decisions, open issues, and dependencies arising from discovery sessions and meetings
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Discovery and clarification sessions involving Business, IT, Card Operations, and Management are ongoing, including agenda items on dual messaging, VISA process adoption, AEP queries, and demand
- Minutes of discussion and progress updates are circulated, but some queries and documentation requests remain open
- A meeting schedule exists for discovery sessions focused on additional requirements for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged cards
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall maintain and execute a structured schedule of discovery sessions with clear agendas, attendees, and expected outcomes for Jaywan requirements
- The bank shall track and manage open questions to AEP and schemes, ensuring timely responses and incorporation into requirements
- The bank shall use a formal change control process to update business requirements and process documents based on discovery outcomes
- The bank shall ensure that key decisions on scope, timelines, and risk acceptance are documented and approved by appropriate governance forums
business_requirements.pre_requisite:

impact_on_operational_process:
- 1. Review current card issuance, transaction processing, and dispute management processes for alignment gaps with Jaywan requirements
- 2. Update card issuance and fulfilment procedures to cater for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged products, including new checks and scheme codes
- 3. Adapt authorization and switching operational runbooks to include Jaywan routing, monitoring, and incident handling procedures
- 4. Define and implement new workflows for Jaywan DMS processing across ATM, POS, e-commerce, and tokenized channels, including file handling and cut-off management
- 5. Enhance reconciliation operations to incorporate Jaywan scheme files, GL mappings, and exception handling routines
- 6. Establish Jaywan-specific procedures for reversals, refunds, and chargebacks including evidence collection, timelines, and escalation paths
- 7. Update call center, branch, and back-office scripts to address Jaywan product features, usage restrictions, and dispute scenarios
- 8. Introduce operational controls and monitoring for Jaywan wallet provisioning and token lifecycle management
- 9. Align operational reporting and daily dashboards to include Jaywan metrics for volumes, failures, and exceptions
- 10. Coordinate with AEP and schemes for incident communication, maintenance windows, and operational readiness reviews
regulatory_impact:
- 1. Comply with CBUAE circular mandating Jaywan co-badged card issuance for licensed financial institutions
- 2. Align transaction routing so that domestic transactions are processed via Jaywan where acceptance infrastructure is available, supporting CBUAE’s domestic scheme objectives
- 3. Implement reporting obligations to CBUAE and AEP using prescribed templates and submission cycles for Jaywan transaction data and scheme participation metrics
- 4. Ensure customer protection and dispute resolution processes for Jaywan meet or exceed CBUAE consumer protection standards and relevant local regulations
- 5. Maintain compliance with CBUAE standards on payment security, data protection, and operational resilience for domestic payment infrastructures
- 6. Facilitate supervisory review and audit by maintaining documentation, logs, and evidence demonstrating full alignment with Jaywan-related regulatory expectations
- 7. Monitor ongoing regulatory updates regarding bilateral agreements (e.g. India corridor), GCC usage, and wallet enablement to update business requirements when formally issued
reports_requirement:
- 1. Regulatory Reports
- - Bank shall produce CBUAE and AEP mandated Jaywan transaction and settlement reports in the required frequency and format
- - Bank shall segregate domestic, GCC, and international Jaywan-related volumes and values where requested by regulators
- 2. Operational and Reconciliation Reports
- - Bank shall generate daily reconciliation reports comparing Jaywan scheme files, internal ledgers, and GL postings
- - Bank shall provide exception reports for unmatched Jaywan transactions, settlement variances, and delayed postings
- 3. Management Information (MI) and Business Reports
- - Bank shall provide dashboards and periodic reports tracking Jaywan adoption, usage by channel, and impact on payment costs
- - Bank shall segment Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged performance by product, geography, and customer segment where data permits
- 4. Risk and Compliance Reports
- - Bank shall incorporate Jaywan transaction flows into AML, fraud, and sanctions monitoring reports, including scheme-specific filters
- - Bank shall monitor and report on Jaywan dispute volumes, reversal trends, and customer complaints for oversight
- 5. Ad-hoc and Analytical Reports
- - Bank shall support ad-hoc analysis requests from Business, Finance, and Regulators related to Jaywan scheme performance and strategic assessment
- - Bank shall ensure underlying data for Jaywan is accessible in the data warehouse for advanced analytics subject to access controls
access_requirement:
- 1. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
- - Bank shall define roles for Jaywan-related functions (e.g. configuration, operations, reconciliation, dispute management) and restrict access accordingly
- 2. Principle of Least Privilege
- - Bank shall ensure users only have access to Jaywan data and functions necessary for their role, minimizing unauthorized exposure
- 3. Segregation of Duties
- - Bank shall segregate duties between configuration, transaction processing, and reconciliation roles for Jaywan to reduce operational risk
- 4. Audit Trails
- - Bank shall maintain detailed logs of user access and changes related to Jaywan configurations, transactions, and reports for audit purposes
- 5. External Partner Access
- - Bank shall control and monitor any access provided to external parties (e.g. service providers) related to Jaywan integrations in accordance with outsourcing and security policies
security_requirement:
- 1. Data Security and Encryption
- - Bank shall ensure that Jaywan cardholder data is protected in line with applicable card security standards and CBUAE regulations, including encryption in transit and at rest
- 2. Tokenization Security
- - Bank shall enforce secure tokenization for Jaywan cards used in digital wallets and e-commerce, ensuring token life-cycle management complies with scheme and bank policies
- 3. Access and Authentication
- - Bank shall ensure strong authentication mechanisms are in place for systems managing Jaywan configurations and operations
- 4. Monitoring and Incident Response
- - Bank shall include Jaywan-related traffic and systems within its security monitoring, SIEM, and incident response frameworks
- 5. Vulnerability Management
- - Bank shall assess and remediate vulnerabilities in Jaywan-related components as part of regular security testing and patching cycles
- 6. Compliance with Regulatory and Scheme Security Standards
- - Bank shall comply with CBUAE, AEP, and relevant international scheme security guidelines for domestic card schemes and co-badged configurations
data_requirement:
- 1. Data Elements and Standards
- - Bank shall capture and store Jaywan-specific scheme identifiers, BIN details, routing flags, and transaction attributes across systems
- 2. Data Quality and Validation
- - Bank shall implement validation controls to ensure accuracy and completeness of Jaywan transaction and customer data
- 3. Data Retention
- - Bank shall retain Jaywan transactional and reference data in line with CBUAE record-keeping requirements and internal policies
- 4. Data Integration
- - Bank shall integrate Jaywan-related data into data warehouse and reporting platforms with clear lineage and transformation rules
- 5. Privacy and Confidentiality
- - Bank shall handle Jaywan-related customer data in compliance with applicable data protection laws and internal privacy standards
- 6. Reference Data Management
- - Bank shall maintain up-to-date reference data for Jaywan products, BINs, fees, and routing parameters in centralized repositories
training_requirement:
- 1. Operational Training
- - Bank shall provide targeted training to Card Operations, GBO-ATM/CDM, Reconciliation, and Dispute Management teams on Jaywan processes
- 2. Frontline Staff Training
- - Bank shall train branch and call center staff on Jaywan product features, usage rules, and common customer queries
- 3. IT and Support Training
- - Bank shall train IT support and monitoring teams on Jaywan system configurations, routing logic, and incident handling procedures
